subject: Design review: Air-gapped HSM escrow shim + periodic shard rotation
messages:
From: MayaCorp Security <security@mayacorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: review of air-gapped HSM escrow shim design

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for agreeing to review our proposed key custody approach. We cut a short draft and a network diagram (attached). High-level ask: confirm that the "escrow shim" model below will meet Redwood's private deployment constraints and our compliance posture. Key points we tried to accommodate:

- HSM is in our on-prem co-lo with no outbound internet (air-gapped).
- A small, auditable bridge appliance (one-way data diode allowed) will accept signed wrap requests from Redwood runtime via a GRPC proxy.
- The HSM will hold a master wrapping key; regular application keys are wrapped and stored in our vault.
- Periodic rotation should be operator-minimal and produce auditable rotation records.

Specific questions:
1) Is a one-way GRPC proxy with mTLS + hardware-backed TPM identity sufficient for the runtime-to-bridge trust?
2) For rotation, we propose a 3-of-5 shard quorum. Can Redwood support automatic rewrap flows when only 2 shards are reachable (fallback policy)?
3) Any objections to using an ephemeral rewrap token (15-minute TTL) derived by the HSM and bound to an audit nonce?

Attached: mayacorp_hsm_airgap_diagram.pdf, draft-ceremony-checklist.md

Appreciate any quick guidance — we have an audit on July 8.

— Keerthi
MayaCorp Security

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: MayaCorp Security <security@mayacorp.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: review of air-gapped HSM escrow shim design

Keerthi — thanks for the clear deck and the diagram. Quick read below, then I'll loop Jordan for orchestration/ops impacts. High-level: approach is reasonable and aligns with how we handle private (VPC/on-prem) BYOK customers, but a few clarifications and one recommend change.

Answers inline:

Q1 (one-way GRPC proxy + mTLS + TPM identity): Yes, that is sufficient in principle. Two points:
- The proxy must do mutual attestation: Redwood runtime certs should be validated against a CA chain that the customer either provides or we pin in the private control plane. TPM-backed identity is good for the bridge appliance attestation step.
- If the bridge is strictly outbound-less, ensure the audit nonce exchange is possible (we typically encode nonces in the wrapped payload so the HSM signs an audit token). If air-gapped entirely, a small courier or USB-signed audit blob works for ceremonies, but that changes automation assumptions.

Q2 (3-of-5 shards + fallback to 2): We can support automatic rewrap when only two shards are reachable, but we must explicitly treat that as "degraded" mode requiring higher MFA/approval. Policy options:
- Auto-rewrap with a policy tag (degraded=true) and retention of pre-rotation ciphertext for 30d.
- Block automatic rewrap and require on-call confirmation (preferred for high-risk customers).

Q3 (ephemeral rewrap token TTL=15m bound to audit nonce): Good pattern. Ensure the token is single-use and the HSM binds the nonce and token expiry inside the signed response. That makes replays nonviable.

Recommendation: add a small HSM-side offline ledger (append-only signed entries) that records rotation events and token nonces. The ledger can be exported periodically as a signed artifact (USB) for auditors. Reduces reliance on continuous networked telemetry and simplifies proof-of-rotation.

Action items (for us):
- Jordan: confirm orchestration on Redwood Dedicated/Private for rewrap retry/backoff rules and degraded-mode handling.
- Jasmine: draft the preflight checklist for the on-prem ceremony (what we need from MayaCorp).
- Priyom: prepare a short note on CA pinning and mutual attestation options for the bridge.

I'll schedule a 30-min sync if helpful.

— Priyom
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: MayaCorp Security <security@mayacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: review of air-gapped HSM escrow shim design

Adding ops detail. We can implement the rewrap flow in the Private control plane with the following constraints and features:

- Connection model: GRPC over a pinned mutual-TLS session. We'll support both a customer-supplied CA bundle and cert-pinning via a fingerprint in the customer config.
- Network: the bridge appliance must expose only the proxy port (no ssh, no management plane). We'll require an IP allowlist and SR-IOV NIC pinning for the bridge VM when deployed in colos that allow it (prevents NIC spoofing).
- Observability: the bridge will emit audit events to a local file rotated daily, plus a signed digest every rotation exported as artifact. If customer allows one-way egress, we can accept push telemetry to our collector across a single outbound channel.
- Rotation flow: Redwood will perform a staged rewrap: 1) request ephemeral token; 2) HSM issues token and signed ledger entry; 3) Redwood performs rewrap and uploads new ciphertext to the customer's vault. For 3-of-5 quorum we implement an explicit quorum-check service.
- Degraded mode: implement a flag on the key metadata (rotation_state=degraded) that prevents automatic key use for non-critical workloads. Customers can opt-in for full auto-rewrap via contract.

Operational ask for MayaCorp: we need one scheduling window (2 hours) for the initial key-ceremony rehearsal and a list of who will hold shards (prefer principle names + contact emails). Please also confirm whether your co-lo supports SR-IOV NIC assignment.

I'll prepare a small runbook and post to the Drive link today.

— Jordan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
